missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.

For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

When testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.

The retro-reflective devices shall have the resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.
The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1.

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1: cycle 1 with a black-standard thermometer (65 ± 3 °C) or cycle 4 with a black-panel thermometer (63 ± 3 °C), exposure periods of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) or 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.
While all other functions with which a lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF, the lamp shall fulfill the photometric and colorimetric requirements.

While specific instructions are absent, the lamp shall not intentionally vary its photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

When there is doubt, the requirement that no red light shall be emitted to the front and no white light shall be emitted to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.
The devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.
All categories of vehicles shall be equipped with two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device.

The S1, S2, S3, or S4 category devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility for S1 or S2 categories devices shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that (a) where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°; (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

The electrical connections for rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, except that if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be permitted to have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The ESA representative of its type shall have measured values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

For pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V (12V system) or +20 V (24V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V (12V system) or +150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

If any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, then the single lamp shall ensure that at least one of the following provisions applies: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
The lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) shall have all measurements made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.

The light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage, within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid.

extra.text: If the rear combination lamp is approved as an electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) under UN R10, an approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to the approved type. No marking is required if the electronics are built into a vehicle that is approved as a unit.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of production samples and drawings: when ESA approval under UN R10 is held, check that the paragraph 5.3 approval mark is present on every unit of the approved type. Pass if the mark is present on all units. If the lamp is covered only by the vehicle's R10 approval, confirm that this is documented.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 10.
extra.test_case: Design review and fitting check of the lamp ESA as installed on the M1 vehicle. Pass if the ESA passes the UN R10 ESA tests (para. 6.1.1.2) and does not cause the vehicle to fail UN R10 radiated emission or immunity limits under normal conditions of use.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be tested for conducted emissions.
extra.test_case: ESA conducted emissions test on the supply lines per the relevant UN R10 annexes, with each lighting function energised. Pass if conducted emissions/transients stay within the specified limits.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
extra.test_case: ESA conducted immunity/transient test on the supply lines per the relevant UN R10 annex, with the functions monitored. Pass if the lighting functions show no malfunction during or after the applied disturbances, according to the agreed functional status.

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement over 75-400 MHz with the lamp functions energised. Pass if all values are below the logarithmically increasing limit line from 52 dBµV/m at 75 MHz to 63 dBµV/m at 400 MHz (Appendix 6).

extra.text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on a 12 V supply with each lamp function switched on and off. Pass if the positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +75 V.

extra.text: When tested by the stripline method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz at 60 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the position, stop or reversing functions over more than 90 per cent of the frequency band.

extra.text: When tested by the stripline method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz at 50 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

extra.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz at 21 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions over more than 90 per cent of the band.

extra.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz at 18 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

extra.text: During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity related functions of the rear combination lamp ESA.
extra.test_case: Monitor each lamp function during all Annex 9 exposures. Pass if there is no unintended switching on or off, no flicker and no change of light output for the position, stop and reversing functions.

extra.text: If the lamp may be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions (e.g. stop lamp) that shall be operational during engine start phases shall meet functional status B when subjected to the starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems) with 10 pulses.
extra.test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II, 10 pulses, per Annex 10; pass if functional status B per ISO 16750-1.

extra.text: If the lamp may be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions that need not be operational during engine start phases shall meet functional status C when subjected to the starting profile at immunity test level II with 10 pulses.
extra.test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II, 10 pulses; pass if functional status C per ISO 16750-1.

extra.text: If the lamp may be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the rear combination lamp functions not related to immunity related functions shall meet functional status D when subjected to the starting profile at immunity test level II with 10 pulses.
extra.test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II, 10 pulses; pass if functional status D per ISO 16750-1.

extra.text: When subjected to test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses, the rear combination lamp shall meet FPSC class III, both for functions related and not related to immunity related functions.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 1, -75 V/-450 V, 500 pulses per Annex 10; pass if FPSC III per ISO 7637-1.

extra.text: When subjected to test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) for 500 pulses, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class I.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a, +37 V, 500 pulses; pass if FPSC I (function performs as designed during and after test).

extra.text: When subjected to test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class II.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b, +10 V/+20 V, 10 pulses; pass if FPSC II.

extra.text: When subjected to test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class I.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a, -112 V/-150 V, 1 h; pass if FPSC I.

extra.text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. or 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Broadband radiated emission measurement per Annex 7 (ESA, 120 kHz bandwidth) across 30-75 MHz with lamp functions energised; pass if all measured values are at or below 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. or 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the constant limit E = 63 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Broadband radiated emission measurement per Annex 7 (ESA, 120 kHz bandwidth) across 400-1,000 MHz with lamp functions energised; pass if all measured values are at or below 63 dBµV/m.

extra.text: When measured according to paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: ESA narrowband radiated emission measurement per paragraph 6.6.2.1. / Annex 8 method, 120 kHz bandwidth, 30-75 MHz; pass if measured level <= 52 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m at every frequency

extra.text: When measured according to paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the constant limit E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: ESA narrowband radiated emission measurement per paragraph 6.6.2.1. / Annex 8 method, 120 kHz bandwidth, 400-1,000 MHz; pass if measured level <= 53 dBµV/m at every frequency

extra.text: The rear combination lamp (ESA) under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
extra.test_case: Check the test report: all lamp functions are energised at nominal supply voltage, preferably all simultaneously at maximum load, during the whole 30-1,000 MHz measurement.

extra.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
extra.test_case: Scan 30-1,000 MHz in an ALSE or OATS; pass if emissions are at or below the para. 6.5 limits across the whole range.

extra.text: If peak detectors are used for the broadband emission measurement of the rear combination lamp, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied to the quasi-peak limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10.
extra.test_case: Review evaluation: peak readings compared against the quasi-peak limit with the 20 dB CISPR 12 correction applied; quasi-peak readings compared directly against the limit.

extra.text: The narrowband radiated emissions of the rear combination lamp ESA shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
extra.test_case: Perform a radiated emission scan from 30 to 1,000 MHz per Annex 8. Pass: the emissions are below the para. 6.6.2.1 narrowband limits across the whole range.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9: absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5, and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
extra.test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm that the chosen ISO 11452-2/-3/-4/-5/-11 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz. Pass: the full range is covered with no gaps.

extra.text: For the immunity tests of the rear combination lamp ESA, the frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check the test setup and report against ISO 11452-1. Pass: the frequency range and general conditions conform.

extra.text: The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check the test software's step and dwell settings against ISO 11452-1. Pass: they conform.

extra.text: Test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the rear combination lamp ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
extra.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b applied to each supply-connected input (e.g. tail, stop, reverse feeds) with lamp operating; functions remain within the immunity performance criteria.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: circle surrounding "E" followed by the country distinguishing number is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4. for the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector functions.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection against paragraph 3.2.4.: a correct identification symbol is present for each approved function.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "148R" followed by the two-digit series of amendments in force at the time of approval.

extra.text: As the rear combination lamp is a handed unit which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of both left- and right-hand units: horizontal mounting arrow present.

extra.text: If the reversing lamp has reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
extra.test_case: If approved with reduced light distribution: check the arrow in installed orientation points outwards from the vehicle.

extra.text: If a lamp function has reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
extra.test_case: If approved with reduced light distribution: visual inspection shows the downward vertical arrow from a horizontal segment.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp shall bear the approval marking.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: approval marking present on the lamp.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: trade name or mark of the applicant present.

extra.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: If applicable: visual inspection of the external unit for identification number and manufacturer name.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number is affixed to the combined lamp complying with several UN Regulations, it shall be visible after installation.
extra.test_case: Inspection on vehicle or mock-up: single approval mark visible after installation.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is used, no part of the combined lamp that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
extra.test_case: Design review and disassembly check: removing any light-transmitting part also removes the approval mark.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the rear combination lamp intended for installation on M1 vehicles, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Review the lamp design and drawings against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes, using the series of amendments in force at application. Check every requirement that can be verified at lamp type approval, e.g. geometric visibility angles, apparent surface and colour. Pass if all such requirements are met.

extra.text: The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 sections 5 and 6 pertinent to the rear position lamp and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied to the rear position lamp function, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Check the rear position lamp's geometric visibility and red colour against the UN R48 individual specification for rear position lamps on M1. Check the illuminating surface and orientation of the handed unit, with the opposite-side unit presumed mirrored. Pass if compliant.

extra.text: The lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions of the rear combination lamp) shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured.
extra.test_case: Design review plus vibration/durability test representative of vehicle use (e.g. per OEM vibration profile); after exposure, all functions (rear position, stop, reversing) operate correctly with no LED failure, intermittent contact, loosened fasteners or mechanical damage.

extra.text: If a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp function, only one logo shall be incorporated, and all requirements of this Regulation for that specific function shall be fulfilled.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection for the number of logos; photometric and colorimetric tests of the function with the logo per this Regulation; pass if there is one logo and all function requirements are met.

extra.text: Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be incorporated in the lamp's optical components or outer lens.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the logo against the vehicle or body manufacturer brand; pass if it is only that brand logo.

extra.text: The stop lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the stop lamp apparent surface (optical components and outer lens); pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the reversing lamp apparent surface (optical components and outer lens window); pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: In the rear combination lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
extra.test_case: Review the circuit diagram and PCB layout to identify LED groups wired in series or with common failure behaviour. Disconnect one LED per group and verify that the whole group extinguishes. Pass: each such group is treated as one light source in the failure analysis of paragraph 4.6.1.2.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.10.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
extra.test_case: Option (a): simulate failure of each single light source (or group per paragraph 4.6.1.1.) in turn and measure on a goniophotometer at the Annex 3 grid points. Pass: all minimum intensities are met; with all sources lit, no maximum is exceeded. Option (b): verify that a failure signal is produced for each single failure. Pass: signal is produced and the communication form notes tell-tale-only use.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2, in case of failure of the variable intensity control resulting in emission of more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control (e.g. open or short of the control input or driver fault) and measure the luminous intensity. Pass: the lamp automatically reverts to intensities meeting the steady-intensity requirements of category R1.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: EMC testing of radiated and conducted (power line) emissions, assessed at vehicle type level (e.g. per UN R10); pass if no malfunction of other vehicle electric/electronic systems is caused.

extra.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module shall not be interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
extra.test_case: Cross-fitting trial of each module into the other module positions of the same housing, with and without tools; pass if modules with different characteristics cannot be interchanged.

extra.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the rear combination lamp shall be met.
extra.test_case: Replace the module with another sample bearing the same identification code and repeat the photometric measurements of UN R148; pass if all photometric requirements are met.

extra.text: In the case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate the lamp with the control gear and settings declared by the applicant during photometry; pass if the operation matches the declaration.

extra.text: If the applicant requests the additional test, the maximum intensity in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd, in order to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear required in UN Regulation No. 48.
extra.test_case: Optional measurement over H 165°–180° outboard and V -2.5° to +5°, optionally including the vehicle body influence; pass if max ≤ 0.25 cd.

extra.text: Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the luminous intensities measured with both lamps on simultaneously and with the rear position lamp on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by ±5° V and ±10° H of the light distribution table; where either lamp contains more than one light source and is considered a single lamp, the values shall be obtained with all sources in operation.
extra.test_case: Measure grid points within ±5° V / ±10° H with stop + position lamps on, then with the position lamp alone, all sources operating; pass if the ratio is ≥ 5:1 at each point.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity requirements of Table 4.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1; pass if all Table 4 values for the declared category (R1 or R2) are met on each sample.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (a) at reference axis; pass if intensity ≥ 4 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady) and is used as a single lamp, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b) in all directions; pass if no value exceeds 17 cd (except as permitted for reciprocal incorporation with stop lamp).

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady) and is marked "D" (paragraph 3.3.2.5.2.), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 8.5∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no value exceeds 8.5 cd.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1 or R2) shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Photometric grid measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (c), Figure A3-I / Table A2-1; pass if each grid point meets the prescribed percentage of the minimum intensity.

extra.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility (paragraph 4.8.3.1 (d)), the rear position lamp (R1 or R2) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement over the full geometric visibility field; pass if intensity ≥ 0.05 cd in all directions.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on the reference axis per para. 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if intensity ≥ 60 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady) and used as a single lamp, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement over the light distribution per para. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no intensity > 260 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady) and is a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 1.30∙10^2 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per para. 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no intensity > 130 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady), the light distribution shall comply with the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)).
extra.test_case: Measure intensities at the grid points of Figure A3-I per para. 4.8.3.1 (c); pass if each point meets the prescribed percentage of the minimum intensity.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady), the luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be not less than 3∙10^-1 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).
extra.test_case: Measure intensity throughout the geometric visibility field of Table A2-1 per para. 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if all values ≥ 0.3 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable), the luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be not less than 3∙10^-1 cd for day condition.
extra.test_case: Measure in day mode throughout the Table A2-1 field per para. 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if all values ≥ 0.3 cd.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall meet the requirements in Table 10, with the standard light distribution as defined in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1 at the Figure A3-V grid points; pass if all Table 10 values are met.

extra.text: The reversing lamp of category AR shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if the minimum luminous intensity is ≥ 80 cd where required.

extra.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR shall not exceed 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b) over all directions in or above the H-plane; pass if maximum ≤ 300 cd.

extra.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR shall not exceed 6.00∙10^2 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b) from H-plane down to 5°D; pass if maximum ≤ 600 cd.

extra.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp of category AR shall not exceed 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b) below 5°D; pass if maximum ≤ 8,000 cd.

extra.text: If the reversing lamp is approved under the pair-only condition, the device shall only be installed on the vehicle in a pair.
extra.test_case: Inspect vehicle installation against communication form paragraph 9.1.3; pass if reversing lamps are fitted as a pair.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Verify failure behaviour per paragraph 4.6 (e.g. simulated LED failure); pass if paragraph 4.6 requirements are met.

extra.text: The angles of geometric visibility of Annex 2 are those for lamps to be mounted on the right side of the vehicle; the handed rear combination lamp for the opposite (left) side shall meet the same angles in the mirrored arrangement.
extra.test_case: Design and drawing review of both handed units against Annex 2 Figures A2-I. Pass if the inboard and outboard directions are correctly assigned for each side.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp (R1, R2) is to be installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 15° above / 5° below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the mounting height is less than 750 mm. Check visibility. Pass if the apparent surface is unobstructed from 15° above to 5° below the H-plane.

extra.text: If the stop lamp (S1, S2) is mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm, the reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 45° outboard may be used, but only below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the H-plane height is below 750 mm. Check visibility below the H-plane. Pass if the apparent surface is unobstructed from at least 20° inboard to 45° outboard.

extra.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Vertical geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Figures A2-I. Pass if the apparent surface is unobstructed from 15° above to 15° below the H-plane.

extra.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall have their direction H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis, which on the vehicle is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, oriented in the required direction of visibility and passing through the centre of reference.
extra.test_case: Review the drawing and mounting data: the reference axis passes through the declared centre of reference and is horizontal and parallel to the vehicle median longitudinal plane in the installed position. Pass if consistent.

extra.text: Unless specified otherwise, the minimum intensities for the various directions of measurement shall be the percentages shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each grid point. Compute each point limit as the figure percentage times the required minimum intensity, rounded down to three significant digits. Pass if every measured value is at least its limit.

extra.text: Where the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the declared mounting height of the H plane. If it is ≤ 750 mm, verify the photometric grid only down to V = -5°. Pass if all points from V = -5° upwards meet their minima.

extra.text: Where the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the declared mounting height of the H plane. If it is ≤ 750 mm, verify the stop lamp grid only down to V = -5°. Pass if all points from V = -5° upwards meet their minima.

extra.text: In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of the lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
extra.test_case: First examine the lit lamp visually. If substantial local variations appear, measure the intensity between adjacent grid directions of Figure A3-V. Pass if each value is at least 50 % of the lower of the two prescribed minima.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (Table 3) according to the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Measure on a goniophotometer at the Figure A3-I grid points. Pass if each point is at least its percentage of the Table 3 minimum.

extra.text: The stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (Table 7) according to the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Measure on a goniophotometer at the Figure A3-I grid points. Pass if each point is at least its percentage of the Table 7 minimum.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall emit, at the measuring points of Figure A3-V (expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference), at least the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Measure on a goniophotometer at each Figure A3-V point relative to the reference axis. Pass if each value in cd is at least the value shown in the figure.

extra.text: With respect to photometric performances, any mass-produced lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric requirements when tested according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of a randomly selected production lamp per paragraph 4.8.; pass if the photometric requirements of the Regulation are met for each function.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by the mass-produced lamp shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples per paragraph 4.9.; pass if the chromaticity coordinates fall within the prescribed colour boundaries for each function.

extra.text: The size of the approval marking shall comply with the value for "a" defined in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Measure the dimensions of the approval mark components against the value of "a" in Table 1. Use the Annex 10 examples as the arrangement reference.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the marking against the approval documents: the circle with "E" and the correct country number must be present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: the sequential number must match the approval number and have 4 to 6 digits.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: the class symbol(s) of the retro-reflector (e.g. IA or IB) must be present and match the approval.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "150R" followed by the correct series-of-amendments digits (e.g. 00) must be present.

extra.text: If the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format of Figure I of paragraph 3.3.3.1.
extra.test_case: Visual comparison of the UI mark with Figure I. The UI number must match the entry in the UN secure internet database.

extra.text: If the retro-reflector is of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the word "TOP" shall be inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Review the retro-reflector's rotational symmetry and the mounting orientation specified by the manufacturer. If orientation is ambiguous, verify that "TOP" is horizontal at the highest part of the illuminating surface.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed to the combined lamp, the marking shall be visible after installation on the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Install the lamp in the vehicle or a representative fixture and confirm the single marking is visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is used, no part of the combined lamp that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Design review and disassembly check: each light-transmitting part (outer lens, reversing insert, retro-reflector) must be inseparable from the part carrying the marking.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall meet the requirements contained in section 5 "General specifications" of UN Regulation No. 48, and the Annexes referenced in that section, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, as pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and to vehicle category M1, where verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Inspect the device and its installation drawings against UN R48 section 5 and the referenced Annexes for M1. Pass if every pertinent requirement that can be verified at device approval is met.

extra.text: The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall meet the individual specifications for this device in section 6 of UN Regulation No. 48, and the Annexes referenced in that section, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for type approval. These specifications cover presence, number, arrangement, position (width, height, length), geometric visibility, orientation and other requirements, as pertinent to vehicle category M1. They apply where verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Check the drawings and the device against the UN R48 section 6 provisions for rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular: mounting height and lateral position, geometric visibility angles and orientation for M1. Pass if all requirements that can be verified at device approval are met.

extra.text: After the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6, and at least one hour after this test, the retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetric characteristics of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI of paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.).
extra.test_case: Heat all ten samples 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C, wait ≥1 h, measure colour and RI at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if colour within red limits and RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx.

extra.text: The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum RI values after the heat test shall meet the complete photometric requirements of paragraph 5.1.4.
extra.test_case: Complete photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 on min and max samples; pass if all Table 3 red values for Class IA/IB are met.

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2. (visual, trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) after each test group; pass if within R48 night-time red limits.

extra.text: Where more than one or a range of different axes of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements with reference to each axis of reference or to the extreme axes of reference of the range specified.
extra.test_case: Repeat photometric measurements for each declared axis / extreme axes of the range; pass if Table 3 values are met each time.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angle β1 = 0°, β2 = 0° shall be equal to or greater than 3.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1.
extra.test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4; pass if RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx.

extra.text: Where the Class IA or IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Confirm declared mounting height of H plane; if < 750 mm, verify Table 3 RI values down to 5° below horizontal only.

extra.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
extra.test_case: Measure trichromatic coordinates per paragraph 4.2.1.; pass if within R48 night-time red limits.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6 for 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C without distortion on visual inspection.
extra.test_case: All ten samples, 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C; visual inspection for distortion; pass if no distortion and subsequent colour and RI comply.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the water test of 10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position, followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Two samples, 10 min normal + 10 min inverted; pass if no water penetration on visual inspection and colour and RI comply.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand exposure to motor fuels for 5 min (Part 1 of Annex 7) and to oils for 5 min (Part 2 of Annex 7), followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Two samples, 5 min motor fuels then 5 min oils; pass if visual inspection satisfactory and colour and RI comply.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 hours, 2 hours interval, 24 hours) and the rear face test of 1 min, followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Two samples, corrosion 24 h + 2 h interval + 24 h, then rear face 1 min; pass if visual inspection satisfactory and colour and RI comply.

extra.text: For testing the retro-reflection, the retro-reflector shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Verify the source calibration certificate confirms CIE Illuminant A (2856 K).

extra.text: If the retro-reflector is a moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C as the heat resistance test procedure.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1: condition the retro-reflector sample in a dry-atmosphere oven at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 consecutive hours; record temperature and duration.

extra.text: After the resistance to heat test, no cracking of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component shall be visible.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection after Annex 6 Part 1 heat test and cooling; pass if no cracks are visible on the device or its optical component.

extra.text: The retro-reflector, being part of a lamp, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.1: remove removable parts, immerse 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C, top of illuminating surface 20 mm below water surface.

extra.text: After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit; if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection after Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.1 immersion sequence; pass: no water visible on the reflecting surface.

extra.text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 3 para. 2.2.4: verify a test duration of 12 h with 12 complete 5/55 min cycles.

extra.text: Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the device, nor shall one be able to form by tapping or tilting the device.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 3 para. 2.2.6: visually inspect the interior for moisture accumulation, then tap and tilt the device; pass if no standing pool of water is present or formed.

extra.text: Since the retro-reflector is combined with a lamp, the rear combination lamp shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
extra.test_case: Remove all removable parts; expose to saline mist 24 h, dry 2 h, expose 24 h (total 50 h); sample must complete test cycle for subsequent evaluation.

extra.text: About five minutes after wiping with the test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 Part 1 para. 1.1(b): visual inspection about 5 min after the fuel wipe. Pass: no apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are acceptable.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and retro-reflector) shall be so fitted on the vehicle that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
extra.test_case: Install the lamp on the vehicle or a representative body fixture with production fasteners; perform vibration exposure representative of normal conditions of use (paras 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1., 2.3.10.2.); afterwards verify mounting position, orientation, geometric visibility and photometric/colour characteristics remain within R48 and component Regulation requirements; pass if no loosening, displacement or loss of compliance.

extra.text: It shall not be possible for the lamps of the rear combination lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
extra.test_case: Design review and physical inspection of the mounting: verify positive locating features (pins/clips/fixed fasteners) define a unique installed position and orientation with no free adjustment; apply handling loads and vibration and confirm no change in aim/orientation; pass if lamp cannot be shifted out of its prescribed position without deliberate tool use.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair (rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors on the left- and right-hand side) shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this estimate is to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.
extra.test_case: Measure the installed positions of the left and right units on the vehicle against the median longitudinal plane using the exterior geometrical form of the lamps; pass if the positions are symmetrical.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
extra.test_case: Compare the external geometry of the left-hand and mirrored right-hand units (drawings/CAD and physical samples); pass if the units are mirror-symmetrical externally, interior structure excluded.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair (left and right rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors) shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
extra.test_case: Measure the colour of emitted/reflected light of each function on left and right units per the applicable colorimetric method; pass if both units meet the same colorimetric requirements for each function.

extra.text: In case of rear lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect the vehicle rear with lamps installed; pass if there are no logos in lamps, or only one lateral logo on each side, or only one central logo.

extra.text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the installation requirements for the paired rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflectors) set out in the preceding paragraphs shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
extra.test_case: Inspect the vehicle drawings and the installed vehicle. Measure the lamp positions relative to the median longitudinal plane, and compare their mounting heights, colours and photometric characteristics. Pass if any deviation from the paired-lamp requirements is limited to what the vehicle's asymmetrical external shape makes unavoidable.

extra.text: The photometric requirements of each lamp function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of each function individually with all other functions of the module switched OFF. Pass: luminous intensities meet the values prescribed for that function.

extra.text: If the lamp is a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d), it shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.; two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces included in the same lamp body and/or having a common outer lens shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system.
extra.test_case: Review of lamp classification and geometric evaluation per paragraph 5.7.2.1. (60 % area or 75 mm gap criterion). Pass: criterion met and the lamp is not declared/approved as an interdependent lamp system on the basis of separate surfaces in a common housing/outer lens.

extra.text: Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (rear position lamp, stop lamp, red retro-reflector) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Vehicle-level check according to paragraph 5.10.4.1 (Zone 1, transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle, Annex 4). Pass if no red light from the rear lamp is visible from the front.

extra.text: For the visibility of red light towards the front of the vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp of the rear combination lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
extra.test_case: Geometric or visual check on the vehicle per Annex 4: observer moved throughout Zone 1 in the transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle. Pass if no part of the apparent surface of any red function is directly visible.

extra.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamp is switched ON and OFF only simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if they exist), the side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp, except while one or more of the conditions of paragraph 5.11.1 exist (position lamps switched ON as parking lamps; side-marker lamps flashing with direction indicators; daytime running lamps switched ON; front position lamp function substituted under paragraph 5.12.1).
extra.test_case: Vehicle-level functional check of the lighting switch circuit: operate the position lamp switch and verify that the rear position lamps, front position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, side-marker lamps (if fitted) and rear registration plate lamp all turn ON and OFF together. Repeat with parking lamps, DRL and paragraph 5.12.1 substitution active to confirm only the permitted exceptions occur. Pass: no state in which any of these lamps can be switched ON or OFF independently outside the 5.11.1 exceptions.

extra.text: The colour of the light reflected by the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
extra.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the retro-reflected light under the standard illuminant according to the retro-reflector colour test procedure; pass if the coordinates lie within the red chromaticity area defined in the Regulation's colour definitions.

extra.text: The number of rear position lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the M1 vehicle installation: count rear position lamps fitted and compare with the number prescribed in the individual specification for rear position lamps (para. 6.10.2); pass if equal.

extra.text: The number of rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the M1 vehicle installation: count rear non-triangular retro-reflectors fitted and compare with the number prescribed in the individual specification for rear retro-reflectors (para. 6.14.2); pass if equal.

extra.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use" (fixed position meaning the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not).
extra.test_case: With the lamp installed on the vehicle, place each movable component in every manufacturer-specified fixed rest position (locked or not) other than the normal position of use; determine the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis that remains unobscured. Pass: no more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface hidden.

extra.text: If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable for the rear position lamp, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.
extra.test_case: Move the movable component to each fixed position where more than 50 per cent of the rear position lamp apparent surface is hidden; verify the additional lamps switch ON automatically and verify by inspection/measurement that they meet the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps. Pass: additional lamps ON and compliant.

extra.text: The rear position lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse; the rear position lamp shall therefore be operable by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.
extra.test_case: Inspect the lamp as installed on the M1 vehicle: with only the light source and/or fuse fitted (no additional wiring, modules or modifications), switch on the rear position lamp function; pass if the lamp operates.

extra.text: If a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is provided, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in colour to the function that has ceased to operate.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of rear position lamp; verify replacement function emits red light within the rear position lamp colour boundaries (R48 / R148 colorimetric requirements). Pass: colour similar (red).

extra.text: If a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is provided, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.
extra.test_case: With replacement active, actuate the replacement device's original function (e.g. braking). Pass: original function operates and meets its photometric requirements.

extra.text: During temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.
extra.test_case: Simulate rear position lamp failure with replacement active. Pass: dashboard tell-tale illuminates indicating temporary replacement and need for repair.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp of category R2 and the stop lamp of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control, they shall respond simultaneously only to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2.
extra.test_case: Review the control strategy and inputs, then trigger each listed environmental and traffic condition. Pass if both lamps respond simultaneously and only to the conditions in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp of category R2 and the stop lamp of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, their intensities shall all vary together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
extra.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity of both functions at several control levels across the full range. Pass if both vary together in the same direction and in a similar proportion.

extra.text: When the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, and if the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop or reversing function) has, according to its type approval documentation, been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the lamp shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant device or function as it has been approved. This does not apply if the device includes an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
extra.test_case: On the vehicle in constant voltage operating condition as specified by the applicant, measure the voltage at the lamp terminals for each function; pass if the voltage does not exceed the voltage stated in the lamp's type approval documentation.

extra.text: In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., for 6 Volt-Systems, the voltage at the terminals of the rear position, stop and reversing lamp device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V by more than 3 per cent, when the vehicle electrical system is in a constant voltage operating condition. This does not apply if the device includes an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
extra.test_case: Measure terminal voltage of each function on the vehicle in constant voltage operating condition; pass if ≤ 6.75 V + 3 per cent.

extra.text: When the rear combination lamp is installed on the vehicle, there shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp to the propagation of light from any part of its apparent surface observed from infinity; obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved are not taken into account.
extra.test_case: Installed-vehicle inspection: observe the apparent surface from infinity (or parallel-shifted directions) over the full geometric visibility angles prescribed for the rear position lamp; pass if no vehicle part obstructs light from any part of the apparent surface, except obstacles present at lamp type approval.

extra.text: If, when the rear combination lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of a lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of the installed (partially masked) unit or with representative masking; pass if the unmasked part meets all photometric values prescribed for approval of each function.

extra.text: If an LED module of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop or reversing function) is not replaceable, this shall be stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval; otherwise the LED module shall be replaceable.
extra.test_case: Document and design review: compare the replaceability of each LED module in the lamp (removal without destroying the lamp) against the component type approval communication sheet (UN R7/R23 or R148). Pass if each non-replaceable LED module is declared non-replaceable on the communication sheet, or if the module is replaceable.

extra.text: If the light-signalling lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.
extra.test_case: Design review for presence of a manufacturer logo in the light-emitting surface; if present, verify the UN R148 approval covers the logo configuration; pass if approval to UN R148 including the logo exists.

extra.text: A reversing lamp shall be mandatorily installed on motor vehicles (including category M1).
extra.test_case: Vehicle installation inspection: verify that at least one reversing lamp function is fitted; pass if present.

extra.text: On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device shall be mandatory and a second device is optional.
extra.test_case: Vehicle installation inspection: count reversing lamp devices; pass if 1 or 2 devices are fitted.

extra.text: For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility angle α shall be 15° upwards and 5° downwards, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check per paragraph 2.10.7: verify unobstructed apparent surface from 15° up to 5° down relative to reference axis; pass if visible throughout.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
extra.test_case: Vehicle installation inspection: verify reference axis of the reversing lamp is directed rearwards.

extra.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
extra.test_case: Check R23/R148 requirements for failure indication; if required, simulate lamp failure and verify tell-tale operates.

extra.text: Stop lamp devices of category S1 or S2 shall be installed on the M1 category vehicle (mandatory).
extra.test_case: Vehicle installation inspection: verify the S1 or S2 category stop lamps are fitted on the M1 vehicle. Pass if present.

extra.text: Two S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be installed on the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Vehicle inspection: count the S1/S2 stop lamps, handed unit plus mirrored opposite-side unit. Pass if exactly two are installed.

extra.text: For M1 category vehicles, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of an S1 or S2 category stop lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Measure on the vehicle, according to R48 para. 5.8 methods, the lateral distance from the outermost point of the stop lamp apparent surface to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. Pass if ≤ 400 mm on each side.

extra.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the vehicle installation. Pass if the lamp is mounted at the vehicle rear.

extra.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
